reason: Objects are retrieved by unique object keys; the value is an object, not a queryable document.
limitation: Not a general-purpose database; field queries need other services.
use_case_why: Large binary objects need inexpensive durable storage and key retrieval, not field-level database queries.

reason: Indexes JSON documents for search; it is not a pure member of the four families.
limitation: Not a transactional system of record.

reason: JSON documents can contain nested fields and be indexed and queried by attributes.
limitation: Cross-document access and indexing require careful design.
use_case_why: Different catalog items have different attributes; indexed JSON supports flexible filtering without a fixed schema.

reason: Rows are keyed and organized into column families, supporting ordered range scans.
limitation: Ad hoc queries across arbitrary fields are difficult.
use_case_why: Sparse timestamped measurements benefit from ordered row-key scans and scalable writes.

reason: Property graphs and RDF graphs support relationship traversals and pattern matching.
limitation: Not ideal for simple high-volume key lookups or tabular aggregation.
use_case_why: Fraud investigations require multi-hop relationship traversal rather than independent record lookups.

reason: A string key maps to an opaque value in memory for rapid retrieval.
limitation: Volatile cache; evictions or restarts can lose data.
use_case_why: Repeated lookups of temporary values benefit from in-memory access; durable storage is unnecessary for a disposable cache.

limitation: Joins and cross-shard queries can cost more.

reason: Keys address values and data structures.
limitation: Memory capacity and durability settings matter.
Queries must be designed around partition keys.
